transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-04-10
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Lena Ortiz (Redwood SE), Noah Kim (Redwood Solutions), Maya Chen (BlueSky Procurement), Danilo Ruiz (BlueSky Legal), Priya Kapoor (BlueSky Platform), Ellen Park (BlueSky Security)

Summary (auto): Procurement and legal alignment; focus on MSA/DPA redlines, SLA appendix for Dedicated / Private, required security artifacts and procurement timeline. Next steps and owners captured.

00:00 - 00:28 Samir Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll run through the governance checklist, this is Samir from Redwood, and I'm joined by Lena and Noah. How's everyone?
00:29 - 01:05 Maya Chen: Hi Samir, thanks, Maya here from procurement. Danilo from legal will chime in, Priya on eng and Ellen for security. Quick ask — this is a procurement gate call, so we want clarity on the contract terms and the final pricing path.
01:06 - 01:38 Danilo Ruiz: Yep, from legal side we want to understand indemnification, liability cap, data processing, and also subprocessors. We got the MSA draft but there are a few redlines.
01:40 - 02:05 Lena Ortiz: Totally, we'll walk through the key MSA items. Quick context: dedicated deployment option includes dedicated GPU pools and VPC peering, we typically include an SLA appendix for uptime and response times.
02:06 - 02:45 Priya Kapoor: On eng side, main concerns are data residency, ability to audit logs, KMS integration, and egress patterns. We need specifics so we can get security sign-off internally.
02:46 - 03:10 Ellen Park: SOC2 is a must, and we need recent pen test summary. Also: can we get an attestation for data deletion and keys?
03:11 - 03:45 Noah Kim: Yes, Ellen, we have a security pack link — I'll paste that in follow-up email. It includes SOC2 Type II, recent pen test summary, and our KMS/HSM integration notes. Also we have a DPA template.
03:46 - 04:30 Maya Chen: Good. On pricing — finance wants to know if we can lock pricing for 12 months and what the PO cadence looks like, are monthly invoices okay or do you need commit?
04:31 - 05:00 Samir Patel: We support both usage-based and reserved committed capacity. For enterprise, we usually do a reserved commitment with monthly invoicing. We can lock list price for 12 months in the SOW.
05:01 - 05:40 Danilo Ruiz: Back to legal: indemnity language — current MSA has mutual indemnification but the liability cap is one year of fees; our legal target is 2x fees or $5M, whichever is lower. Is that something you've seen accepted?
05:41 - 06:15 Lena Ortiz: We've negotiated caps in prior deals; 2x fees is a common ask. We may need to check with contracts but we can propose compromise language in the redline.
06:16 - 07:00 Priya Kapoor: Technical question — for private deployments, how do you handle KV cache persistence and backups? We need to ensure no PII is cached in persistent stores.
07:01 - 07:30 Lena Ortiz: Good point. Our runtime supports configurable KV cache policies; for private/VPC we can disable persistent caching for tokens and use in-memory only, and we document safe defaults in the deployment guide.
07:31 - 08:10 Ellen Park: And encryption at rest? Is it customer-managed keys (CMK) via KMS?
08:11 - 08:45 Noah Kim: Yes, for Private we support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM integrations. We'll include the KMS integration notes in the package.
08:46 - 09:20 Maya Chen: Procurement process question: after legal signs off, procurement needs a PO and vendor onboarding form. We need lead times for onboarding — how long from signed MSA to production access?
09:21 - 09:55 Samir Patel: Typical onboarding for Dedicated is 4-6 weeks: contract, provisioning, networking setup, and integration tests. For hosted API it's faster. We'll outline onboarding milestones.
09:56 - 10:30 Danilo Ruiz: Regarding DPA — we need data residency clauses for EU data and an export control clause. Also subprocessors list and notification windows for changes.
10:31 - 11:05 Lena Ortiz: The DPA template includes standard SCCs and subprocessor disclosures; we can mark any specific subprocessors if required. We generally give 30 days' notice of new subprocessors.
11:06 - 11:55 Priya Kapoor: A practical ask: can you provide an SLA appendix that includes latency SLOs for 95th pct under our expected burst profile? Our feature is latency sensitive.
11:56 - 12:30 Lena Ortiz: We can provide latency profiles tied to model families and token lengths. For Dedicated we can commit to P95 latency targets and provide credits for missed SLOs. We'll show sample numbers in the SLA appendix.
12:31 - 13:25 Maya Chen: For procurement sign-off, finance needs to know the escalation path and who signs PO — do you do purchase orders or platform invoices tied to a contract?
13:26 - 14:00 Samir Patel: We accept POs against the master agreement; invoices can be monthly. For larger reserved commitments, we sometimes require a deposit or initial invoice on signing.
14:01 - 14:50 Danilo Ruiz: On IP — we want a clear carve-out that customer data remains customer property and model outputs are owned by customer. Any default IP assignment language?
14:51 - 15:30 Noah Kim: Redwood's standard is customer retains rights to their data and outputs. We'll call this out in the MSA/SOW. We can add explicit language in the redline.
15:31 - 16:20 Priya Kapoor: Can we get a short-run benchmark? We want to run a perf check on our prompt sets before committing. Is a limited-time pilot possible?
16:21 - 17:00 Lena Ortiz: Yes, we can do a pilot. Typical approach: 2-week pilot on dedicated small pool or hosted with quota, share perf spreadsheet and test harness. We'll need an NDA if there are sensitive prompts.
17:01 - 17:45 Maya Chen: Finance also asked about taxes and export compliance — do you have standard tax forms and W9?
17:46 - 18:20 Samir Patel: We'll provide W9 and tax details. For export, we have compliance docs and can include relevant attestations.
18:21 - 19:30 Danilo Ruiz: A couple redlines in the MSA we sent: 1) change notification period from 30 to 60 days for service changes, 2) stronger data deletion verification, 3) limit on subcontractor access to production data.
19:31 - 20:10 Samir Patel: Those are reasonable to discuss. We can propose 45 days for changes or commit to notice plus mitigations. For subcontractors we can add tighter controls and SCAs.
20:11 - 21:00 Ellen Park: On audit rights — can we get a right to audit or at least a SOC2 attestation and the option for a third-party assessment under NDA?
21:01 - 21:40 Noah Kim: SOC2 Type II report is available; for third-party assessments we typically do carve-outs and offer audit windows under NDA. We'll capture this in the DPA appendix.
21:41 - 23:00 Priya Kapoor: On network setup — we need specifics for VPC peering, allowed CIDR, egress ports, and typical IP ranges for Redwood egress. That will go into our infra ticketing.
23:01 - 23:45 Lena Ortiz: We'll provide a network runbook with the egress IP ranges and port list. For dedicated we also support private connectivity options.
23:46 - 25:10 Maya Chen: Can you confirm backups and retention policies? We have retention limits due to health data, even if not PHI some teams are strict.
25:11 - 25:50 Noah Kim: Retention policies are configurable for private deployments. For hosted we have default retention; we'll include retention SLAs and deletion procedures in the DPA.
25:51 - 27:00 Danilo Ruiz: About the SLA credit model — is it linear or stepwise? Also need to know the cap on credits and whether credits apply to committed fees.
27:01 - 27:40 Lena Ortiz: Usually credits are percentage-based per SLA window and apply against monthly invoices up to a cap (often 10-25% of fee), but we can propose language aligned to your procurement policy.
27:41 - 29:00 Maya Chen: Procurement needs a checklist of what to attach to the purchase order: signed MSA, SOW (with SKU list), W9, insurance cert, vendor onboarding form. Do you have a vendor portal?
29:01 - 29:45 Samir Patel: We don't have a portal for PO uploads yet; we accept POs via email to billing@redwood.example and can provide a vendor onboarding form. We'll include insurance and W9 in the security pack.
29:46 - 31:20 Priya Kapoor: Small point — do you do RBAC integrations and SCIM for user provisioning? We need SCIM for automatic provisioning.
31:21 - 32:00 Noah Kim: Yes, we support SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning for enterprise accounts; we'll include docs and examples.
32:01 - 33:10 Danilo Ruiz: Any unusual export-control clauses? We're regulated in EU and US, need to ensure no surprise export obligations.
33:11 - 33:55 Lena Ortiz: Standard export control language is in our MSA; nothing unusual. We'll flag the export control clause for your legal review.
33:56 - 35:00 Maya Chen: Timeline check — procurement needs to close by end of month for budget. If legal + security sign off this week, will procurement be able to issue PO by 2025-04-22?
35:01 - 35:40 Samir Patel: That's feasible if legal redlines come back quickly; we'll prioritize contract review. We'll aim to deliver redlined MSA and DPA by 2025-04-14.
35:41 - 36:30 Danilo Ruiz: Request: include a versioned list of subprocessors in the DPA and a commitment to notify via email 30-45 days before onboarding new subprocessors.
36:31 - 37:10 Noah Kim: We'll commit to 30 days and provide a versioned subprocessor list in the DPA.
37:11 - 38:00 Priya Kapoor: For pilot perf testing, what's the mechanism for telemetry? We'll need logs and token-level latency metrics.
38:01 - 38:35 Lena Ortiz: We can provide token-level latency breakdowns via the Console and a sample tracing hook. We'll share a perf spreadsheet.
38:36 - 39:30 Maya Chen: One last ask: on SLAs for privacy incidents — notification windows and breach handling steps.
39:31 - 40:10 Ellen Park: Yes, incident response times, notification within 72 hours, ability to accept forensic help.
40:11 - 40:50 Noah Kim: We have incident response SLAs; notification commitments are usually 72 hours for confirmed breaches and we provide forensics under NDA.
40:51 - 41:30 Samir Patel: Ok to recap — Redwood will send: redlined MSA + DPA draft, SLA appendix and sample latency/credit language, security pack (SOC2 + pen test + KMS notes), perf baseline spreadsheet, network runbook, and vendor onboarding form.
41:31 - 42:15 Maya Chen: Great. Action owners noted. We'll aim to circulate internal legal redlines by 2025-04-16 and procurement will confirm PO timeline after that.
42:16 - 43:00 Danilo Ruiz: Quick note — liability cap target is 2x fees / $5M max; we'll include rationale with redlines.
43:01 - 44:00 Priya Kapoor: We'll schedule a follow-up technical deep dive once contracts are near final to review onboarding steps and run the pilot.
44:01 - 44:45 Samir Patel: Sounds good. I'll set up a follow-up tech deep dive and pilot kickoff slot.
44:46 - 46:00 Maya Chen: Thanks everyone. Please include contact for billing and legal in the follow-up email.
46:01 - 47:10 Samir Patel: Will do. Thanks all.
47:11 - 47:50 (meeting close)

Artifacts referenced:
- MSA v1 (sent prior) - link: https://redwood.example/msas/redwood-msa-v1.pdf
- DPA template - link: https://redwood.example/legal/dpa-template.pdf

- SLA appendix sample - link: https://redwood.example/sla/sla-sample.pdf
- Perf baseline spreadsheet (to be shared) - note: Samir/Lena will attach post-call
